result.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
result.summary: GUI memory should preserve the results of past actions and learn reusable operations. This is difficult in long-horizon workflows, where agents must use information across applications and useful operations are interleaved with failed attempts. We introduce Task Advancement Memory (TAM), which defines task advancement as verified task progress, and supports ongoing task execution and learns reusable operations. During execution, Task Advancement State represents how verified task progress changes the remaining goals, allowing the agent to build on earlier achievements across applications. After each task, advancement supervision identifies and abstracts the interactions that produced a verified local result. The learned operations preserve the relation between required inputs, expected outcomes, and verification conditions. This retains locally successful operations from both successful and failed tasks. On MobileWorld GUI-only tasks, Advancement State alone raises success from 12.0% to 28.2%. Full TAM achieves a 17.6% relative gain in task success over the strongest evaluated baseline and reduces lifecycle tokens per solved task by 38.7%. On SPA-Bench, TAM achieves state-of-the-art task success in the single-app English Level 3 setting.

AI.brief_summary: 该文面向长时程 GUI 智能体提出 Task Advancement Memory：执行期用「任务推进状态」表示已验证进度如何改变剩余目标，任务结束后通过推进监督抽取可复用的局部操作，并保留成功与失败任务中的有效交互，在 MobileWorld 等基准上报告了成功率提升与 token 下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「已验证进度」状态更新与从交互中抽象可复用操作的监督方式，可能为 LVR 中的状态维护、视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的借鉴线索，但论文本身未涉及 latent 推理或内部表示分析。
